newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Q1 GDP, Michigan data slated.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Q1 GDP, Michigan data slated.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities are expected to show little movement on Friday, said market participants who continued to await the results of next week's policy-making Federal Reserve meeting.

The final reading on real first quarter gross domestic product was scheduled for release Friday and economists polled by Reuters expected, on average, a 5.9 percent increase would be seen along with a 2.8 percent rise in the price index. The University of Michigan's final June reading on consumer confidence also was due and seen marginally higher at 103.5.
He pointed to a strong Tankan report from Japan and the tightening of interest rates by the Bank of Canada as pressures weighing on the market.
"You now have a global economy where pressure on interest rates (can come from abroad)," he said.

The GDP revisions to be seen on Friday will be old news and have little market-moving impact, Berner said, as inflation remained well behaved. He said the market would be more concerned with anticipating results of the NAPM and nonfarm payrolls reports next week, when the bond market will be closed Friday and end early on Thursday.
